Subject: PO requirements and invoice frequency for reserved capacity discount

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement has two quick gating items before we can issue a blanket PO: 1) we need the exact PO header fields that must appear on invoices (company legal name + tax ID + bill-to entity), and 2) confirmation of the invoice cadence that Redwood will accept. Our AP team can only process monthly statements (one invoice per month) unless we provide a signed exception.

Also — the discount band you quoted mentions a 10% reserved-capacity credit that is triggered by 'committed spend >= $150k per quarter'. We need that to be converted into clear billing rules in the PO (do we net the credit onto the monthly invoice, or is it issued as a quarterly credit note?). Can you attach your preferred PO template and confirm how credits will appear on invoices?

I attached our PO template (AlphaGrid_PO_Template.pdf) and a stub of the commitment schedule. If we can get narrow answers on the PO fields + credit handling this week, procurement can circulate the blanket PO and we can close the commercial steps.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Hi Lydia —

Thanks for the note and for sending the PO template — that helps a lot. Short answers up front:

- Required invoice PO fields: Redwood can accept the AlphaGrid_PO_Template fields you sent. We require the PO number, bill-to entity, tax ID, and billing address in the invoice header for AP reconciliation. If you attach a PO with those fields populated we can map it to our billing system automatically.

- Invoice cadence: Redwood's standard billing for reserved capacity is monthly invoicing. We can also support a single quarterly invoice if the customer requests it and the procurement team provides the signed exception. Note that quarterly invoices affect how discounts/credits are applied (see below).

- Discount / credit mechanics: For the reserved capacity credit (10% at >= $150k/Q), Redwood can apply that as either: (A) a monthly pro rata credit applied to each monthly invoice within the quarter (reduces the monthlies), or (B) a consolidated credit note issued at quarter close that is netted on the next invoice. We prefer option (A) for bookkeeping simplicity, but we can agree to (B) if AlphaGrid requires a single credit document for controls.

I'm cc'ing Vanessa (your Redwood AM) and Ben (billing) to confirm operational steps and the timeline for the PO. Vanessa — can you confirm whether there are any price/packaging rules that change if AlphaGrid requests quarterly invoices instead of monthly? Ben — any mapping notes we should share for the PO fields so procurement can populate the PDF correctly?

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-14T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice frequency for reserved capacity discount

Hi Lydia —

Quick clarification on packaging & discounting so procurement can sign off: the 10% reserved-capacity discount is tied to committed spend tiers in the commercial schedule (AG-2028-058). That tier is evaluated on a quarterly basis. Operationally we handle it two ways (as Sofia noted):

- Monthly pro rata: we divide the committed discount across the three monthly invoices for the quarter. This is simplest for AP and keeps month-to-month cashflows predictable.
- Quarterly credit note: we invoice full list prices monthly and then issue a single credit note at quarter end for the realized discount amount.

Important: if AlphaGrid opts for a single quarterly invoice instead of monthly statements, the quarterly invoice will reflect the net discounted amount for the quarter (no separate credit note necessary). However, our finance team needs the signed exception flagged on the PO so we can set the billing schedule in our ERP.

Ben — can you confirm PO field mapping for their template? If procurement fills the AlphaGrid_PO_Template with the PO number, bill-to name, tax ID, and billing address in the header we should be able to auto-link it. Also confirm what PDF meta field we should read for your AP system (PO-number vs reference-id).

Lydia — if you prefer, I can draft the exact clause text to include in the PO to avoid back-and-forth with your legal team. Example clause: "Discount eligibility and crediting will be evaluated quarterly; discounts will be applied pro rata to monthly invoices unless AlphaGrid requests a consolidated quarterly invoice, in which case the invoiced amount will reflect the net quarterly discount."

Thanks — happy to put that clause into the PO template for you.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
